blocks.orig: Tingatinga art is a unique and vibrant painting style. Developed in the second half of the 20th century in Tanzania, the bold art form soon developed across other destinations in East Africa. The Tanzanian art of Tingatinga was borne from a simple idea. Use recycled, low-cost materials like masonite squares, ceramic fragments and bicycle paint and transform them into beautiful art. The result is something special.
blocks.html: Tingatinga is a distinctive, colourful style of painting. It emerged in Tanzania during the second half of the 20th century, and this bold art form quickly spread to other parts of East Africa. The Tanzanian Tingatinga tradition grew out of a straightforward idea: take cheap, recycled materials such as masonite squares, bits of ceramic and bicycle paint and turn them into beautiful artwork. What comes out is something quite special.

blocks.orig: Tingatinga paintings are typically striking in colour due to being painted on masonite. Whether painted on canvas, wood, or mottled watercolour paper, however, Tingatinga paintings have a tactile quality that sets them apart. Traditionally painted on small surfaces and incorporating bold and colourful depictions of flora and fauna of Tanzania, Tingatinga art pieces are effortless to transport. As such, over the past 100 years, the uniquely African style of art has become one of the most loved Tanzania souvenirs. Today, Tingatinga has developed to incorporate modern techniques, different materials and a wide range of sizes.
blocks.html: Because they are painted on masonite, Tingatinga paintings usually have strikingly strong colours. Yet whether the surface is canvas, wood or mottled watercolour paper, Tingatinga works have a tactile feel that makes them stand out. As they are traditionally painted on small boards and show bold, colourful scenes of Tanzania’s plants and animals, Tingatinga pieces are easy to carry home. That is why, over the last 100 years, this uniquely African style has grown into one of the best-loved souvenirs from Tanzania. Today Tingatinga has evolved to take in modern techniques, other materials and a broad range of sizes.

Tingatinga Paintings: keeping a legend alive

blocks.orig: The founder of Tingatinga Paintings, Edward Tingatinga, was born in the settlement of Mindu in the 1930s. Looking at a road map of Tanzania today, this location cannot be found. In fact, there is not much left of this settlement itself, and the house where he was born is now unfortunately wholly gone. However, the legend of this talented African artist still lives on in The Tingatinga Arts Cooperative Society.
blocks.html: Edward Tingatinga, the founder of Tingatinga Paintings, was born in the 1930s in the settlement of Mindu. You will not find that place on a present-day road map of Tanzania. Little of the settlement remains, and sadly the house where he was born has disappeared entirely. Even so, the legend of this gifted African artist lives on in The Tingatinga Arts Cooperative Society.

blocks.orig: Also sometimes referred to as the Tingatinga School, the Tingatinga Arts Cooperative Society is located alongside Morogoro Stores in Tanzania’s capital. The creative cooperative hosts around 100 talented artists who use art to express their creativity and talent through these colourful art pieces. Many artists see themselves as Tingatinga’s successors and maintain the founder’s style. Others experiment with new forms and motifs, resulting in a beautifully varied and evolved offering to art-lovers.
blocks.html: The Tingatinga Arts Cooperative Society, sometimes known as the Tingatinga School, can be found next to Morogoro Stores in Tanzania’s capital. Around 100 gifted artists work within this creative cooperative, expressing their talent and creativity through these colourful pieces. Many of them regard themselves as Tingatinga’s heirs and keep to the founder’s style, while others try out new forms and motifs, giving art lovers a wonderfully varied and evolving range.

blocks.orig: The objective of the Tingatinga Arts Cooperative Society is to promote the lively, magical, unique beauty of Tanzanian culture. On the one hand, the creative cooperative operates as a painting school for the Tingatinga style. On the other, it promotes art sales internationally to enable its members to earn their living.
blocks.html: The aim of the Tingatinga Arts Cooperative Society is to promote the lively, magical and unique beauty of Tanzanian culture. On one side, the cooperative runs as a school for painting in the Tingatinga style; on the other, it markets the artwork internationally so that its members can make a living.
